lead: one sentence in a yard at twenty-four, half a joke about how poor you both were: nothing goes out of here under a single name. his hands stopped at fifty-one. nothing at that bench has stood still since.
sun: you said it and he agreed to it, and a sentence given that way is not the kind that gets looked at again, so nobody has looked at it. terms drawn up between two makers now govern one of them, and the clause that was the generous half at the time is the whole of the arrangement, and neither man has ever mentioned it.
moon: the hands do not slow down to make a point. work leaves the bench at the rate it always has, whether or not what stands behind it is level, and every piece goes out labelled the way that sentence said it would, by you, with no bad grace on any of it. the one lever in the building has never been picked up.
pull: everything that leaves here goes out under two names, and one pair of hands has made all of it for eleven years, and the arrangement that decided that was four seconds long.
tension: the trade assumes there is a document, because nothing that has held this long is thought to run on a spoken sentence, and a spoken sentence is what it runs on. the offers keep arriving — your own shop, your name over the door — and go back inside a day, which reads either as a man with no ambition or as a man being kept. neither of those can be argued down without the other one landing.
cost: a workshop thirty years old with no bad quarter in it is a rare thing, and this one stands on a promise rather than a partnership agreement, which is why no solicitor has been in the building. ending it is what is not available. no sentence exists that would start that, and the bad years came and went without the question ever taking a shape you could put to him.

lead: it is the standard thing in its field, your name is at the top of it, and the reason nothing is locked down is a sentence said to one woman in a corridor before any of this existed.
sun: she was standing exactly level with you the afternoon you gave it, and the thing was two years old and worth nothing, so it was not much of a promise at the time. nothing entered on purpose comes back round for amendment, and it has never been amended. what it obliges is upkeep, with no end date on it, at whatever size the thing turns out to reach.
moon: The Jewel sends work out finished and bare, and the year in which somebody normally puts terms on a piece this visible came and went with no part of you registering that there was anything to do. the promise then closed the question for good. what would read, in another life, as a maker who never thought of it, is here a term being kept exactly.
pull: the most visible thing you have made stands in the light with nothing over it, and what holds it there is a sentence given once, at eye level, to somebody who never asked for it.
tension: a large firm ships it now under its own name, and strangers write to correct you about your own working, and both of those sit inside the terms rather than against them. generous is the word that comes back, which credits a disposition. the accurate version needs a corridor produced, and a woman produced, and a sentence repeated aloud twenty years after the only two people present had agreed it was nothing.
cost: people build on it because it has not moved under them in twenty-two years and will not, which is a rarer property than the work. it has also grown to a size nobody in that corridor imagined. the terms did not grow with it, and no wording of that sentence covers a thin year, so the thin years get covered by you, unmentioned.

lead: nobody can say what you do or which room you are in. four people, in four towns, can give the exact wording of something you told them, and three of the four have been holding it more than twenty years.
sun: each of those was addressed to a person and to nothing else. no firm stands behind them, no body would enforce them, nobody countersigned — the whole weight sits on the fact that you said it, in a room, at an hour you can name. it has held every time, which is the only kind of holding you have ever had occasion to test.
moon: no post, no roll, no address: The Veil left all of that unissued. you did not decline the firms and the committees; the question of joining arrived in a form you had no answer to, and went. the only true facts about you are private ones, each of them held by a single person who has no way to check it against anything.
pull: you can be described by nobody and quoted exactly by four people. everything you are actually in was entered out loud, to one person, with no third party in the room.
tension: two of them met for the first time at a funeral, and each had spent decades holding a version in which they were the arrangement. neither was wrong about their own terms. unattached is the word that follows you, said warmly, usually by somebody with a mortgage and a leaving date — the exact inverse of the position, and correcting it would mean naming the other three.
cost: nobody has ever had to check on you, because nothing was propping any of it — no payroll, no name on a door, no room that would notice a lapse. each of them held anyway. a post can be resigned. a membership runs out. an undertaking made standing in a doorway has no shape that ends it, and yours are all still running.

lead: your sister has your word that this will not be settled cheap. your brother has had your word since the pair of you were twenty-two. neither has been taken back, and both of them are about the same estate.
sun: the heat went out of this in the third year and the case did not slow by a week. what you told her was said at a table, deliberately, with her looking at you, and a thing entered that way stops depending on how you feel about it. the other side has spent nine years waiting you out on a temperature that stopped being involved a decade ago.
moon: his calls come at eleven at night and you take them, you drive him to the appointments, and you go into the room the following week and give nothing back on the terms. neither of those is a gesture toward the other. the second grip has not slackened to make room for the first; they were entered eleven years apart and are both being kept to the letter.
pull: the fight stopped running on anger in year three and did not slow. you are pressing a claim against a man you have not let go of, and both grips were promised out loud.
tension: her reading is that you have not got it in you, delivered kindly and then less kindly. his side reads the visits as work being done on him ahead of a settlement. each of those needs only one of the two to be real, and both are. saying the true thing requires telling your sister that the man she is fighting is somebody you are keeping, and no version of that sentence survives her kitchen.
cost: the claim is intact in its twelfth year and so is he — nothing dropped on either side, no year in which one got traded for the other. these are decided by whoever goes the whole distance first, and you go it twice, in opposite directions. the thing has run past the point where the money would have changed anyone's life, and the ones it was for are old now.
